item.title: Proposed laws for publishing a blyg When botference publishes a blyg post for…
item.description:
Proposed laws for publishing a blyg

When botference publishes a blyg post for its owner, it makes promises. The laws page writes each promise as one sentence. For each law, it says where the promise comes from and how it is checked today.

These laws are proposals. The owner has not adopted any of them. Only the owner can adopt, edit or reject a law; an AI may only propose one.

Each law starts with "For every". For example, one law says that a run of the draft-filling script leaves the draft file exactly as the owner left it. Fifteen laws were proposed on 26 November 2026.

Some laws are not checked by a test yet, and the page says so for each one. An adopted law will get an independent check, written from the law and not from the code. A copy of the laws for review is in the repository, at docs/laws.md.

item.title: Release note: Discuss reads and publishes blyg posts During the Blygger…
item.description:
Release note: Discuss reads and publishes blyg posts

During the Blygger hackathon, 20–27 November 2026, botference's browser extension, Discuss, learned to read blyg posts and to publish them. Blygger is an open protocol for small blogs that quote each other by reference. A post on such a blog is a blyg post. This note lists what changed. The Blygger page describes it in more detail.

Reading a blyg post

  • Quote by reference. On a blyg post, the extension reads the post's own documents. Each highlight then records the post's id and version. The extension tells you when a highlight is not word for word in the post.
  • Responses. On a blyg post, a thread that you publish is a response to that post by default. You can untick this.
  • Mentions. A mention is the notice that tells another blog about your response. Discuss does not send it. Your site's own publisher sends it after the post is live. The Hub, a private feed of the blygs you follow, lists the mentions that your own site receives.

Writing with an agent

  • Agent passages in a marked box. Type /tk-claude or /tk-codex and an instruction in your own comment. The agent writes that passage, and the extension shows it in a box marked as an AI's text. The box stays when you publish. The instruction is not published.
  • Drafts with fill-gap. The command botference fill-gap fills one gap in a draft that you write in Obsidian. A site's own scripts call it and keep the answer in a separate file. The draft itself is not changed.

Publishing

  • The publish queue. Every press of the publish button is accepted at once. Posts go out one at a time, in the order you pressed them, up to 20 waiting.
  • One-click publishing. With confirm: never, the press is the publish. A post stops for your look only when publishing would lose something already published.
  • Copy for Blygger Studio. If you write in Blygger Studio, copy the thread as Studio's own markdown and paste it there.

All of this is experimental. The only example set-up is one Jekyll site. Publishing runs your site's own commands, which check, build and push the post. The set-up is in docs/blygger.md.

item.title: botference is five tools Botference runs Claude Code and Codex side by side. It…
item.description:
botference is five tools

Botference runs Claude Code and Codex side by side. It uses the command-line tools that you already have, on your own computer. It started as a planning council. It now holds five tools, and you can use each one alone.

  • Council. You, Claude and Codex plan in one chat, in your terminal. A bot can hand the floor to the other bot, so the two argue a point before they come back to you. Planning is the most mature part of botference.
  • Discuss. A browser extension and a small local server, the companion. Highlight a passage on any web page, write a comment, and mention @claude, @codex or @all. The bots answer in the same thread, at the side of the page.
  • Document review. Margin comments on a LaTeX or Markdown source, rendered as a web page. Tag a bot in a comment, and it answers or suggests a change.
  • Blygger publishing. Publish a Discuss thread to your own site as a blyg post. This part is experimental.
  • Agent tools. botference see takes a phone and a desktop screenshot of a page for a coding agent. botference service keeps a server running after the agent's shell ends.

One person builds botference for their own work, so some parts assume that person's set-up. The home page says who each tool is for and how ready it is. The source is on GitHub, under the MIT license.

This blyg holds release notes and short posts about botference. It is itself made by a small script in the repository, from Markdown files.
